relevance_note: Narrative review of published HA20 patients ('We summarized the literature on patients with HA20 resulting from TNFAIP3 mutations'), mostly aggregate (Table 1), but it gives individual-level clinical detail for four previously published patients (two allogeneic HCT recipients, one autologous HCT recipient, one East Asian patient with Hodgkin lymphoma); no specific variant is attributed to any individual.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; JSON assembled with a short Python script (values typed from my reading, no table transcription) and every span checked verbatim against the Markdown by script. Individuals: only people described individually with clinical detail were given rows; all are previously published cases, so source_reference_in_review is filled. Aggregate Table 1 counts (74 East Asian, 51 other-region patients) were not split into people. n_patients_reported = 125 is the sum of the two stated counts (74 + 51); the paper never states a combined total. The two allogeneic HCT patients are cited jointly as (31, 47); the paper does not attribute one reference to each, so both refs are given for both boys. Within the paper, the single East Asian anti-IL-1 (canakinumab) patient (47) and the single East Asian patient with elevated ISG expression (47) are very probably 'The second case' (Japanese boy treated with canakinumab), but this is not stated, so no separate rows were created and nothing was merged beyond that boy's own description. 'One patient with HA20 in East Asia' (Hodgkin lymphoma, ref 10) could overlap with another individual; not stated. Ages '14-year-old' and '6-year-old' are the only ages given and were recorded as age at last evaluation; they may be ages at HCT. is_proband left null (review; no proband/index designation). Variants: the paper names variants only at study/family level (Cys243Tyr (45), Glu192Lys (18), Met476Ile (20), Arg183X in two families (22, 27), Arg87X (21, 42), p.Asn102Ser, c.487-1G>A, p.Val309dup, Phe127Cys polymorphism), none attributed to an individual described here, so the variants table is empty. Checklist mapping was conservative: 'cell depletion' (not mapped to autoimmune cytopenia), 'hepatitis' (not stated autoimmune), 'enteropathy' and 'bowel disease' (not stated as ulceration/inflammation), and 'Hodgkin lymphoma' (not mapped to lymphoproliferation) left 'not reported'; 'insulin-dependent DM' mapped to type 1 diabetes; 'psoriasis' mapped to skin lesions; 'frequent fever' to recurrent fever; CNS vasculitis to both CNS involvement and vasculitis. No exclusions recorded (no individual-level negative statements). Inconsistencies in the paper: (1) 'four potential splice site mutations or duplication mutations (shown in red squares)' but then 'One of these mutations was reported in Japan (16), while four were reported in China (25, 27)' (1 + 4 = 5); (2) Table 1 recurrent stomatitis in other regions '42/51 (82.6%)' (42/51 is 82.4%); (3) the reviewed studies are given as refs (10–44), yet patients from refs 45 and 47 are also discussed.

study_type.span: In this review, we summarize the characteristics of patients with HA20 in East Asia

n_patients_reported.span: A total of 74 patients in 39 families were affected by HA20 in East Asia, while a total of 51 patients in 23 families were affected by HA20 in other regions.

cites_prior_report_of_same_patients.span: We summarized the literature on patients with HA20 resulting from TNFAIP3 mutations starting from the first report of this disease in 2016 until August 2021.

prior_report_citation.value: (10–44); also (45) and (47) cited for individual patients
span: A total of 20 studies in East Asia and 15 studies in other regions, mainly the USA and Europe, were published during this period (10–44).
